world.name: Hangul Garden
world.tagline: Meet the letters and read your first words

lessons.title: Basic vowels
lessons.concept: Hangul is the Korean alphabet. Each syllable is a block. A vowel alone is written with **ㅇ** in front, which is silent at the start: 아 is just “a”.
lessons.example: 아 · 어 · 오 · 우 · 으 · 이 (a · eo · o · u · eu · i)

lessons.title: Basic consonants
lessons.concept: Put a consonant in front of a vowel to make a syllable block: **ㄱ + ㅏ = 가** (ga). Read the block from left to right.
lessons.example: 가 · 나 · 다 · 마 · 바 · 사 · 하 (ga · na · da · ma · ba · sa · ha)

lessons.title: First words
lessons.concept: Join syllable blocks to make words. Read each block, then say them together.
lessons.example: 우유 (uyu) = milk / 나무 (namu) = tree

lessons.title: Y-vowels
lessons.concept: Adding a short stroke makes a **y**-sound: ㅏ → ㅑ (ya), ㅓ → ㅕ (yeo), ㅗ → ㅛ (yo), ㅜ → ㅠ (yu). ㅐ (ae) and ㅔ (e) sound very similar in modern Korean.
lessons.example: 야 · 여 · 요 · 유 (ya · yeo · yo · yu)

lessons.title: More consonants
lessons.concept: ㄹ is between “r” and “l”. ㅈ (j), ㅊ (ch, with a puff of air), ㅋ (k, with a puff of air), ㅌ (t, with a puff of air) and ㅍ (p, with a puff of air) complete the basic consonants.
lessons.example: 라 · 자 · 차 · 카 · 타 · 파 (ra · ja · cha · ka · ta · pa)

lessons.title: Doubled consonants
lessons.concept: ㄲ, ㄸ, ㅃ, ㅆ and ㅉ are tense sounds: say them with a tight throat and no puff of air, like the first sound in “skate”.
lessons.example: 까 · 따 · 빠 · 싸 · 짜 (kka · tta · ppa · ssa · jja)

lessons.title: Final consonants
lessons.concept: A consonant under the syllable is called **받침 (batchim)**. It closes the syllable: 안 (an), 말 (mal), 밤 (bam), 강 (gang), 집 (jip), 책 (chaek). Only seven sounds are possible at the end: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅇ.
lessons.example: 안 · 말 · 밤 · 강 · 집 (an · mal · bam · gang · jip)

lessons.title: Everyday words
lessons.concept: Read each word syllable by syllable. 학교 is read “hakgyo”: the final ㄱ of 학 is closed and the next syllable is pronounced tightly.
lessons.example: 사과 (sagwa) = apple / 학교 (hakgyo) = school

lessons.title: Words about the world
lessons.concept: People and nature: 사람 (person), 나라 (country), 하늘 (sky), 산 (mountain), 강 (river), 꽃 (flower).
lessons.example: 사람 (saram) = person / 꽃 (kkot) = flower

world.name: Hello Harbor
world.tagline: Say hello, thank you and nice to meet you

lessons.title: Hello and thank you
lessons.concept: Polite greetings end in **-요** or **-니다**. 안녕하세요 works any time of day.
lessons.example: 안녕하세요. (annyeonghaseyo.) = Hello. / 감사합니다. (gamsahamnida.) = Thank you.

lessons.title: Yes, no and okay
lessons.concept: Short polite answers you can use every day. Korean adds **요** at the end to be polite.
lessons.example: 네. (ne.) = Yes. / 아니요. (aniyo.) = No.

lessons.title: Nice to meet you
lessons.concept: When you meet someone new, say 만나서 반갑습니다. There are two ways to say goodbye: one for the person leaving, one for the person staying.
lessons.example: 만나서 반갑습니다. (mannaseo bangapseumnida.) = Nice to meet you.

lessons.title: Polite expressions
lessons.concept: Use 실례합니다 to get someone's attention or pass by, 고마워요 to thank someone in a friendly way, 천만에요 to answer thanks, and 축하해요 to congratulate.
lessons.example: 실례합니다. (sillyehamnida.) = Excuse me. / 고마워요. (gomawoyo.) = Thank you. (friendly)

lessons.title: Names and countries
lessons.concept: Ask a name with 이름이 뭐예요? and a country with 어느 나라 사람이에요? Answer with 제 이름은 ___예요 or 저는 ___ 사람이에요.
lessons.example: 이름이 뭐예요? (ireumi mwoyeyo?) = What is your name?

lessons.title: Saying goodbye
lessons.concept: Among friends you can say 잘 가요 (goodbye), 내일 봐요 (see you tomorrow), 또 만나요 (see you again) and 잘 자요 (sleep well).
lessons.example: 잘 가요. (jal gayo.) = Goodbye. (friendly) / 내일 봐요. (naeil bwayo.) = See you tomorrow.

lessons.title: How are you?
lessons.concept: Ask 잘 지냈어요? (Have you been well?) and answer 잘 지내요 (I'm doing well). 좋은 아침이에요 means “It's a good morning.”
lessons.example: 잘 지내요. (jal jinaeyo.) = I'm doing well.

lessons.title: Asking for help
lessons.concept: Say 도와주세요 to ask for help, 모르겠어요 when you do not know, 알겠어요 when you understand, and 다시 말해 주세요 to ask someone to say it again.
lessons.example: 도와주세요. (dowajuseyo.) = Please help me. / 알겠어요. (algesseoyo.) = I understand.

lessons.title: Likes and answers
lessons.concept: 좋아요 means good or fine, 싫어요 means you don't like it, 맞아요 means “that's right” and 틀려요 means “that's wrong”.
lessons.example: 좋아요. (joayo.) = It's good. / 싫어요. (sireoyo.) = I don't like it.

lessons.title: Signs you will see
lessons.concept: Short signs are everywhere in Korea. **입구** is the entrance, **출구** the exit and **화장실** the restroom. On doors, **미세요** means push and **당기세요** means pull.
lessons.example: 입구 (ipgu) = Entrance / 출구 (chulgu) = Exit

lessons.title: Thank you for the meal
lessons.concept: Before a meal say **잘 먹겠습니다**, and when you finish say **잘 먹었습니다**. A host welcomes you with **어서 오세요**, and **맛있어요** praises the food.
lessons.example: 잘 먹겠습니다. (jal meokgetseumnida.) = Said before eating: “I will eat well.” / 잘 먹었습니다. (jal meogeotseumnida.) = Said after eating: “I ate well.”

courses.title: Korean Level 3 · Me and My Family

world.name: Family Village
world.tagline: Introduce yourself, your family and numbers

lessons.title: I am a student
lessons.concept: **저는** means “I” (polite). Put **이에요** after a consonant and **예요** after a vowel to say “I am …”.
lessons.example: 저는 학생이에요. (jeoneun haksaengieyo.) = I am a student.

lessons.title: My family
lessons.concept: Family words are used a lot in Korean, even for people who are not family.
lessons.example: 가족 (gajok) = family / 어머니 (eomeoni) = mother

lessons.title: Counting
lessons.concept: Korean has two number systems: native Korean (하나, 둘, 셋 …) for counting things, and Sino-Korean (일, 이, 삼 …) for money, dates and minutes.
lessons.example: 하나 · 둘 · 셋 (hana · dul · set)

lessons.title: Native numbers 6–10
lessons.concept: Continue the native Korean numbers: 여섯 (6), 일곱 (7), 여덟 (8), 아홉 (9), 열 (10).
lessons.example: 여섯 · 일곱 · 여덟 · 아홉 · 열 (yeoseot · ilgop · yeodeol · ahop · yeol)

lessons.title: Sino-Korean numbers
lessons.concept: Sino-Korean numbers: 일 (1), 이 (2), 삼 (3), 사 (4), 오 (5), 육 (6), 칠 (7), 팔 (8), 구 (9), 십 (10). They are used for money, dates, phone numbers and minutes.
lessons.example: 일 · 이 · 삼 · 사 · 오 · 육 · 칠 · 팔 · 구 · 십 (il · i · sam · sa · o · yuk · chil · pal · gu · sip)

lessons.title: Age
lessons.concept: Ask 몇 살이에요? (How old are you?). Ages use native numbers plus 살: 열 살 (10 years old), 스무 살 (20), 서른 살 (30).
lessons.example: 몇 살이에요? (myeot sarieyo?) = How old are you?

lessons.title: People
lessons.concept: 친구 (friend), 의사 (doctor), 사람 (person), 남자 (man), 여자 (woman).
lessons.example: 친구 (chingu) = friend / 사람 (saram) = person

lessons.title: More family words
lessons.concept: Siblings use different words depending on who is speaking: a woman says 오빠 (older brother) and 언니 (older sister). Also 아들 (son), 딸 (daughter), 부모님 (parents).
lessons.example: 오빠 (oppa) = older brother (said by a woman) / 언니 (eonni) = older sister (said by a woman)

lessons.title: Our family
lessons.concept: Koreans often say 우리 (we, our) instead of “my”: 우리 가족 means “my family”. Count people with 명: 네 명 (four people).
lessons.example: 우리 가족 (uri gajok) = our family

lessons.title: Texting a friend
lessons.concept: Text messages use short polite sentences ending in **-요**. **지금 어디예요?** asks where you are, **곧 가요** means “I’m coming soon” and **늦어요** means “I’m late”.
lessons.example: 지금 어디예요? (jigeum eodiyeyo?) = Where are you now? / 곧 가요. (got gayo.) = I’m coming soon.

lessons.title: Reading words aloud
lessons.concept: When a syllable ends in a consonant and the next one starts with a vowel, the sound moves over: 책이 is read **chaegi** and 밥을 is read **babeul**. Some sounds also change their neighbours: 국물 is read **gungmul** and 같이 is read **gachi**.
lessons.example: 책이 (chaegi) / 밥을 (babeul)

world.name: Daily Town
world.tagline: Talk about what you do every day

lessons.title: Everyday verbs
lessons.concept: Polite present-tense verbs end in **-아요 / -어요 / -해요**. The same form is used for “I”, “you” and “they”.
lessons.example: 먹어요. (meogeoyo.) = (I) eat. / 마셔요. (masyeoyo.) = (I) drink.

lessons.title: Going to places
lessons.concept: Put **에** after a place to say where you go or come: 학교에 가요. The verb comes last.
lessons.example: 학교에 가요. (hakgyoe gayo.) = I go to school.

lessons.title: Eating, drinking, reading
lessons.concept: The object of a verb gets **을** after a consonant and **를** after a vowel: 밥을 먹어요, 커피를 마셔요.
lessons.example: 밥을 먹어요. (babeul meogeoyo.) = I eat a meal.

lessons.title: Food and drink
lessons.concept: 밥 (rice, a meal), 빵 (bread), 과일 (fruit), 고기 (meat), 물 (water), 우유 (milk).
lessons.example: 빵 (ppang) = bread / 과일 (gwail) = fruit

lessons.title: Likes and dislikes
lessons.concept: Say what you like with -를/을 좋아해요 and what you don't like with -를/을 싫어해요: 저는 사과를 좋아해요.
lessons.example: 좋아해요. (joahaeyo.) = I like it.

lessons.title: Describing things
lessons.concept: Describing words also end in -요: 커요 (big), 작아요 (small), 많아요 (many), 맛있어요 (delicious), 예뻐요 (pretty).
lessons.example: 커요. (keoyo.) = It's big. / 작아요. (jagayo.) = It's small.

lessons.title: Weather
lessons.concept: 날씨 (weather), 더워요 (it's hot), 추워요 (it's cold), 비가 와요 (it's raining), 눈이 와요 (it's snowing).
lessons.example: 더워요. (deowoyo.) = It's hot. / 추워요. (chuwoyo.) = It's cold.

lessons.title: Saying no with 안 and 못
lessons.concept: Put **안** before a verb to say you don't do something (안 가요). Put **못** before it to say you can't (못 가요).
lessons.example: 안 먹어요. (an meogeoyo.) = I don't eat.

lessons.title: Daily routine
lessons.concept: 일어나요 (wake up), 씻어요 (wash), 일해요 (work), 자요 (sleep). Time words such as 아침 (morning) and 밤 (night) take 에: 아침에.
lessons.example: 일어나요. (ireonayo.) = I wake up.

world.name: Time Station
world.tagline: Say what you did and what you will do

lessons.title: Yesterday, today, tomorrow
lessons.concept: Time words usually come near the start of the sentence.
lessons.example: 어제 · 오늘 · 내일 (eoje · oneul · naeil)

lessons.title: What I did
lessons.concept: Past tense: **-았어요 / -었어요 / -했어요**. Some verbs shorten: 가다 → 갔어요, 보다 → 봤어요.
lessons.example: 먹었어요. (meogeosseoyo.) = I ate.

lessons.title: What I will do
lessons.concept: Use **-(으)ㄹ 거예요** for plans: 가다 → 갈 거예요, 먹다 → 먹을 거예요.
lessons.example: 내일 갈 거예요. (naeil gal geoyeyo.) = I will go tomorrow.

lessons.title: Days of the week
lessons.concept: 월요일 (Mon), 화요일 (Tue), 수요일 (Wed), 목요일 (Thu), 금요일 (Fri), 토요일 (Sat), 일요일 (Sun).
lessons.example: 월요일 · 화요일 · 수요일 (woryoil · hwayoil · suyoil)

lessons.title: Months
lessons.concept: Months are a Sino-Korean number plus 월: 일월 (January), 삼월 (March), 오월 (May), 칠월 (July), 구월 (September), 십이월 (December).
lessons.example: 일월 · 삼월 · 오월 (irwol · samwol · owol)

lessons.title: Telling the hour
lessons.concept: Hours use native numbers plus 시: 한 시 (1:00), 두 시 (2:00), 세 시 (3:00), 열 시 (10:00). Ask 몇 시예요?
lessons.example: 한 시 · 두 시 · 세 시 (han si · du si · se si)

lessons.title: How often
lessons.concept: 매일 (every day), 자주 (often), 가끔 (sometimes), 항상 (always). Place them before the verb.
lessons.example: 매일 (maeil) = every day / 가끔 (gakkeum) = sometimes

lessons.title: More past tense
lessons.concept: The past ending is -았/었어요: 했어요 (did), 왔어요 (came), 만났어요 (met), 샀어요 (bought), 잤어요 (slept).
lessons.example: 했어요. (haesseoyo.) = did

lessons.title: Birthdays and weekends
lessons.concept: 생일 (birthday), 주말 (weekend), 선물 (gift). Ask 생일이 언제예요? and answer 제 생일은 오월이에요.
lessons.example: 생일이 언제예요? (saengiri eonjeyeyo?) = When is your birthday?

world.name: Seoul Street
world.tagline: Shop, ask the way and say what you want

lessons.title: At the shop
lessons.concept: Ask the price with 얼마예요? and ask for something with **… 주세요** (… please).
lessons.example: 얼마예요? (eolmayeyo?) = How much is it?

lessons.title: Where is it?
lessons.concept: Ask **… 어디예요?** (Where is …?). Listen for 오른쪽 (right), 왼쪽 (left) and 직진 (straight).
lessons.example: 화장실이 어디예요? (hwajangsiri eodiyeyo?) = Where is the restroom?

lessons.title: I want to …
lessons.concept: Add **-고 싶어요** to a verb stem to say what you want to do: 가다 → 가고 싶어요.
lessons.example: 가고 싶어요. (gago sipeoyo.) = I want to go.

lessons.title: At a restaurant
lessons.concept: 메뉴 (menu), 주문할게요 (I'll order), 물 더 주세요 (more water, please), 계산해 주세요 (the bill, please).
lessons.example: 계산해 주세요. (gyesanhae juseyo.) = The bill, please.

lessons.title: Getting around
lessons.concept: 버스 (bus), 지하철 (subway), 택시 (taxi), 기차 (train). Say how you go with -로/으로: 버스로 가요.
lessons.example: 버스 (beoseu) = bus / 지하철 (jihacheol) = subway

lessons.title: Phone calls and messages
lessons.concept: 전화 (phone call), 전화번호 (phone number), 문자 (text message). 전화해요 means “I call”.
lessons.example: 전화 (jeonhwa) = phone call

lessons.title: At the hospital
lessons.concept: 병원 (hospital), 약 (medicine), 아파요 (it hurts). Say the body part first: 머리가 아파요 (my head hurts).
lessons.example: 병원 (byeongwon) = hospital / 아파요. (apayo.) = It hurts.

lessons.title: Polite requests
lessons.concept: -세요 and -아/어 주세요 make polite requests: 앉으세요 (please sit), 기다려 주세요 (please wait), 문을 열어 주세요 (please open the door).
lessons.example: 기다려 주세요. (gidaryeo juseyo.) = Please wait.

lessons.title: Making plans together
lessons.concept: 같이 (together) invites someone: 같이 가요. 갈래요? asks “Do you want to go?” and 시간 있어요? asks “Do you have time?”
lessons.example: 같이 가요. (gachi gayo.) = Let's go together.
